summary.headline: White House launches voluntary pre-release testing for frontier AI
summary.body: The US administration finalised a voluntary framework under which labs can submit closed frontier models for government safety testing up to 30 days before release; open-weight models are excluded. That strengthens Alignment & Control and Global Coordination, which lifts Gatekeeper and Protector God and pulls Conquerors and Self-Destruction down. Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Max and pledged open weights, spreading capability more widely. Texas froze new data-center approvals pending a grid audit, a sign of Tech Backlash that lifts Reversion, though the exact date of that report is uncertain. Horizon Balance improved to -0.11.
summary.movers_note: Gatekeeper +0.5, mostly from the White House testing framework (+0.47), partly offset by fading earlier news (-0.04). Conquerors -0.4, mostly from the White House testing framework (-0.35) and fading earlier news (-0.04). Protector God +0.3, mostly from the White House testing framework (+0.35), partly offset by fading earlier news (-0.04).

events.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Max and pledges open weights
events.summary: Alibaba made Qwen3.8-Max widely available, claiming it rivals OpenAI, Anthropic and Kimi K3, and said it will publish the weights.
events.reason: Self-reported frontier-class Chinese model; weights only promised.

events.title: Texas freezes new data-center approvals pending grid audit
events.summary: Governor Greg Abbott halted approval of new data-center projects until an audit of their grid connections. Date uncertain: Texas Tribune report dated Aug 3; Wikipedia lists Aug 10.
events.reason: Large US state pauses AI infrastructure.
